newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc stocks low but Chinese arrivals overhang.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc stocks low but Chinese arrivals overhang.

text.p: Movements of zinc stocks caught the eye of London Metal Exchange (LME) market operators over the past week as parcels of material believed to be of Chinese origin moved into Singapore warehouses.
Total LME zinc inventories at 423,250 tonnes are around their lowest levels since December 1992, although traders and market analysts were alert to a further flow of Chinese material.
Around 10,000 tonnes of this origin metal was put on warrant in Singapore this week, against pockets of only small withdrawals elsewhere.
"Chinese exports are likely to be much bigger than the market currently anticipates," broker Macquarie Equities said in their weekly commentary.
"This is due to sales of off grade zinc from government stockpiles in reaction to the recent rise in prices," Macquarie added.
According to the broker Chinese exports in January to April were 162,145 tonnes, (up 131 percent year on year), compared with 226,777 tonnes in the whole of 1996.
Macquarie had previously assumed exports of 300,000 tonnes for 1997 but are now considering raising their estimates to 400,000 tonnes.

Referring to the movements of zinc into Singapore LME brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a report, "this is not unexpected considering the high zinc price and comes at a time when the zinc market had become saturated and in need of a corrective pullback."

Nickel stocks after small falls at the beginning of the week registered a sizeable rise of 1,092 tonnes on Friday. Traders said they believed that the material had been previously uncut material put on warrant.
World nickel stocks at over 12 weeks consumption are well above the seven-week critical point.

Macquarie said that Russian first quarter output was 51,700 tonnes, with exports at 50,140 tonnes. "The export figure suggests Russian de-stocking of between 7,000 and 9,000 tonnes in the first quarter they said.
Aluminium stocks had a string of falls netting 15,550 tonnes on the week.
Total LME stocks standing at 740,400 tonnes are around the lowest since April 1996.
Traders and chartists said that the overall world stock/consumption ratio is less than eight weeks and pegged seven weeks as critical. Exchange stocks are expected to show further falls next week.

Despite a small gain in copper stocks on Friday the overall trend of the week was down. In a recent report Rudolf Wolff said commercial stocks of copper equal just 3.8 weeks of consumption, compared to what brokers consider the "critical level" of five weeks.
Copper stocks are expected to decline again next week, traders said.
